scenario: [LNUL.4.10]: when both operands of a non-connective operator fault, the expression yields the one [LNUL.4.2]'s order selects, and position never enters. The operator is `==` over two Bool operands, each of which faults while it is evaluated: `p.a // p.z > 0` traps (DIVIDE_BY_ZERO, raised inside the operand), and `p.body.name > 5`, a String in a Json slot compared with an Int, raises a TypeError (raised inside the other operand). The kind order ranks the TypeError first. Two rules put the trap on each side of `==`, so a runtime that yields the LEFT fault (or records both) fails at least one. Each fault is an OPERAND's: a mismatch raised by performing the operator itself (`p.a // p.z < p.body.name`) would not count, because [LNUL.4.10] performs no operation once an operand has faulted. Its twin LNUL.4.10.trap_beside_a_type_error_records_no_trap pins that the trap is not recorded ([LERR.1.4.11]). Path: the non-connective BINOP arm -- libds rete/eval.c BINOP (both operands evaluated with faults held, ds_rete_held_select), Mercury ds.eval.m eval_node(e_binop(...)) (lnul_4_10_yielded).
rules_ds:
schema Payload scope logical:
    body: Json key
    a: Int mutable
    z: Int mutable

rule trap_left:
    Payload p where (p.a // p.z > 0) == (p.body.name > 5)
->
    log info "left"

rule trap_right:
    Payload p where (p.body.name > 5) == (p.a // p.z > 0)
->
    log info "right"
